pharm: Echinocandin that inhibits fungal cell wall 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthesis; fungicidal against Candida species, given IV.
quick: Candidemia: 200 mg IV load, then 100 mg once daily
Limited data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
Limited data; consider benefit/risk; poor oral bioavailability
No adjustment needed; monitor liver tests
summary: Anidulafungin (ERAXIS) is an IV echinocandin antifungal for candidemia and other Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess, peritonitis) in adults and children 1 month and older, and for esophageal candidiasis in adults. It is given once daily after a loading dose, needs no renal adjustment, and is unique among echinocandins in undergoing slow non-enzymatic chemical degradation rather than hepatic metabolism, giving it minimal drug interactions.
indications: Candidemia in adults and pediatric patients 1 month of age and older
Other Candida infections - intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis (adults and children 1 month and older)

dosage.d: 200 mg load Day 1, then 100 mg once daily
dosage.n: Continue at least 14 days after last positive culture

dosage.d: 3 mg/kg load (max 200 mg), then 1.5 mg/kg (max 100 mg) daily
dosage.n: At least 14 days after last positive culture

dosage.d: 100 mg load Day 1, then 50 mg once daily
dosage.n: Minimum 14 days and at least 7 days after symptom resolution; high relapse rate

admin: For IV infusion only after reconstitution and dilution per label
Do not exceed an infusion rate of 1.1 mg/minute (about 84 mL/hour)
Reconstitute with sterile water; dilute in 5% dextrose or 0.9% sodium chloride
Do not co-infuse with other medications or electrolytes in the same line unless compatibility is established
No loading-dose adjustment needed for renal or hepatic impairment
moa: Inhibits glucan synthase, the enzyme complex that forms 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall; the resulting cell wall damage is fungicidal against Candida species.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to anidulafungin or other echinocandins
Known or suspected Hereditary Fructose Intolerance (the IV product contains fructose/excipients)
relative: Neonates <1 month (polysorbate 80 toxicity risk; not approved)

preg: Limited human data; animal studies showed skeletal/developmental effects at high doses. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Limited data; anidulafungin is present in animal milk. Oral bioavailability is negligible; consider maternal need and infant exposure.
renal: No dose adjustment required in any degree of renal impairment, including dialysis; anidulafungin is not dialyzable.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required for mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment; monitor liver tests as hepatic adverse effects can occur.

minor: No clinically significant interaction with cyclosporine, voriconazole, tacrolimus, amphotericin B, or rifampin
interactions.diagnostics: Anidulafungin is not a substrate, inducer, or inhibitor of CYP enzymes; minimal drug-drug interaction potential.

serious: Infusion-related reactions (rash, urticaria, flushing, bronchospasm, hypotension)
emergency: Severe infusion reaction with bronchospasm and hypotension

monitoring: Signs/symptoms of infusion-related and hypersensitivity reactions
counsel: This antifungal is given through a vein, once daily
Tell your team if you feel flushing, itching, rash, or trouble breathing during the infusion
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness
Inform your clinician if you have hereditary fructose intolerance
Complete the full course even if you feel better
pk: Steady state reached on first day after loading dose
Refrigerate 2-8 C; reconstituted/diluted solution per label timing
pearls: Unique elimination by slow non-enzymatic chemical degradation, not hepatic metabolism - minimal drug interactions
No dose adjustment for renal or hepatic impairment; not dialyzable
High relapse rate in esophageal candidiasis - reserve and consider alternatives for maintenance
Slow the infusion to under 1.1 mg/min to limit histamine-mediated infusion reactions
missed: Hospital-administered once daily; if a dose is delayed, give as soon as possible and resume the daily schedule. Do not double doses. Managed by the clinical team.
overdose: No specific antidote; anidulafungin is not dialyzable. Doses up to 400 mg as a single load have been given without serious events. Provide supportive care and monitor liver tests.
